evidence: src/application/order-service.ts: OrderService.addProduct checks `!id.trim() || !name.trim() || !Number.isSafeInteger(stock) || stock < 0` and throws `new DomainError("Product requires an id, name, and non-negative integer stock")`, so a domain rule about products is written in the application service.

src/application/order-service.ts: OrderService.placeOrder checks `product.stock < item.quantity` and then changes stock directly with `product.stock -= item.quantity`, with no domain operation involved.

src/application/order-service.ts: OrderService.cancelOrder changes stock directly with `product.stock += item.quantity` and runs no validation, so the stock rule is handled differently in each method.

src/application/order-service.ts: order changes go through domain functions `createOrder`, `transitionOrder`, `cancelOrder`, but product changes do not, so the service uses the domain abstraction for one aggregate and not the other.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit is one file with one concern: order fulfilment orchestration over the FulfilmentStore port. It handles the two aggregates in different ways, though. Orders go through domain operations (createOrder, transitionOrder, cancelOrder from ../domain/order), so their rules stay in the domain. Products are built and changed inline in the service. addProduct writes out the product validity rule itself (non-blank id and name, non-negative safe-integer stock) and throws the domain's DomainError for it. It also builds the product object before checking it. placeOrder checks stock against quantity and subtracts with `product.stock -= item.quantity`. cancelOrder adds stock back with `product.stock += item.quantity` and runs no check. As a result, the stock rules are split across three methods in the application layer instead of living behind one product abstraction, and the service treats the domain inconsistently. This matches the rubric's fail conditions: a scattered invariant and a bypassed abstraction. Confidence is moderate because src/domain/product.ts is not shown, so I can't confirm that the domain already has a product factory or stock operation being duplicated.

violations.message: Product rules (id and name required, non-negative integer stock, enough stock, decrementing and restoring stock) are written inline in OrderService.addProduct, placeOrder and cancelOrder, and DomainError is thrown from the application layer. Orders go through domain functions (createOrder, transitionOrder, cancelOrder), but products skip any domain abstraction, so the stock rule is split across several methods instead of living in one place.
